text.text_excerpt: Stumbled on this place while in route to subway! Man am I happy that this happened! I got the southwest panini (chicken, red onion tomato and the special chipotle sauce) all of that for $6.50! It a good size panini enough for lunch that's for sure! The other person in the party got the pesto chicken panini (chicken, pesto tomato, armed onion and lettuce) some of the best pesto she has had to date. I recommend it if your in the area! There is plenty of room to sit down inside so bring your crew!

This is one of the only nearby lunch options for LSUHSC students, and it's a great one! They make the most delicious smoothies of any place I've tried in the city, that actually taste like fresh tropical fruit. The sandwiches and wraps are tasty too, and the prices for combos are really reasonable. It's refreshing to for a place in New Orleans to not have gut-busting portions, but my only complaint is that I wish they would stuff their sandwiches and wraps with more veggies. As for the service, the counter people are always friendly, a refreshing break from the moody workers at some establishments. Also, if I'm not mistaken, this place is also black-owned, which is all too rare in this city.

I was surprised the first time I stopped at this small cafe and how many items were on their menu. On my first visit I got a smoothie and it was tasty and fresh. On my next visit I got the veggie panini deal which added a bag of chips and instead of a bottled soft drink, I chose a fresh brewed tea (sweet & unsweet available). Service is pretty quick and there are a few tables to dine in, although I brought mine selection back to work. Yes the parking lot is kind of odd; the whole lot is a weird shape, but since I walk over from work it's not an issue. Good alternative to the chain sandwich place next door.
